items.title: Building Europe’s CO₂ infrastructure: The EU regulatory framework and managing cross-chain risks
items.summary: Online webinar on 27 November 2026 (10:00–11:00), organised by CCUS Innovation, Bellona and Carbon Management Europe, on the EU regulatory challenges and opportunities for CO₂ transport and storage infrastructure. It discusses how an EU-wide framework could support investment, enable cross-border transport and create a European CO₂ market ahead of the Commission's CO₂ Infrastructure and Markets legislation, expected in early 2027, as well as the impact of transport and storage disruptions on emitters and possible EU-level risk-sharing such as an EU Guarantee Mechanism. Speakers are Aymeric Amand (Carbon Management Europe), Tom Mikunda (Bellona Europa) and Marton Volstad (CCUS Innovation).
items.why_it_matters: The coming CO₂ Infrastructure and Markets law will set third-party access, tariff and cross-chain liability rules that shape cross-border Nordic CO₂ flows and the risk allocation assumed in network-design models.

items.title: Can CCS stop the AI boom from blowing the carbon budget?
items.summary: SINTEF news item noting that data centres could account for 7 per cent of global electricity demand. At the UN climate summit COP31, SINTEF's Mona Mølnvik argued that gas power with carbon capture is a possible solution, provided that solutions that cannot be fixed afterwards are not locked in. (Summary from the SINTEF feed; the page could not be opened.)
items.why_it_matters: Gas power with CCS to supply data centres would add a new class of CO₂ sources that Nordic transport and storage networks would have to collect, which changes demand scenarios for hub and storage capacity planning.
